payload.description: Read crypto-core/sha256.mjs, crypto-core/sha256.test.mjs, and crypto-core/keccak.mjs in full to establish house style (pure-JS lane arithmetic, header comment conventions, export shapes) and the verification standard (compare against node:crypto, hardcode published known-answer values, print 'N pass, M fail', process.exit(fail?1:0)).
payload.result: Confirmed sha256.mjs uses Uint32Array/>>>0 arithmetic for 32-bit words; keccak.mjs uses BigInt with a 64-bit mask for 64-bit lanes. Adopted the same split for sha512.mjs and blake2.mjs.

payload.description: Listed the proofbundle repo tree, read cli/proofbundle-cli.mjs and package.json to understand the keygen/seal/verify commands, and read (read-only, not modified) mlkem_scaffold_agent_worklog.json / mlkem_scaffold_agent_aibom.json as a format precedent for another agent's provenance files.
payload.result: Confirmed CLI usage: 'node cli/proofbundle-cli.mjs keygen|seal|verify'. Confirmed no forbidden files (mlkem*, keccak*, sha256*, other agents' *_agent_* files) would be touched.

payload.description: Checked which hash algorithm names and options node:crypto exposes in this environment (Node v24.18.0 / OpenSSL 3.5.7).
payload.result: 'sha512','sha384','blake2b512','blake2s256' all work for default parameters. createHash('blake2b512',{outputLength:N}) throws 'not XOF or invalid length'. The {key} option is silently ignored (a 100-byte, spec-invalid key produced byte-identical output to no key). Concluded keyed/variable-length BLAKE2 needed independent KAT sources rather than a live Node oracle.

payload.description: Wrote a throwaway BigInt script (scratchpad/gen_sha512_constants.mjs, not part of the deliverable) that derives SHA-512's K[80]/H0 and SHA-384's H0 from first principles per FIPS 180-4 4.2.3/5.3.4/5.3.5 (fractional parts of cube/square roots of primes via exact integer isqrt/icbrt), rather than transcribing the constants from memory.
payload.result: Cross-validated the derivation method by reproducing SHA-256's K and H0 with the same code and diffing against the already-trusted literals in crypto-core/sha256.mjs: exact match. Also verified structurally that the high 32 bits of each of the first 64 SHA-512 K words equal the corresponding SHA-256 K word. Used the derived hex literals directly in sha512.mjs.

payload.description: Fetched RFC 7693 raw text (rfc-editor.org) for the exact SIGMA permutation table, G mixing function, F compression function pseudocode, and parameter-block layout; fetched a NIST-vector mirror (di-mgt.com.au) for SHA-384/512 known-answer values (empty string, 'abc', the 112-character multi-block message, one million 'a' characters).
payload.result: Confirmed SIGMA/G/F pseudocode matches what was implemented. Cross-verified every fetched NIST vector against a live node:crypto computation before hardcoding it (all matched exactly), including the million-'a' stress vectors for both SHA-512 and SHA-384.

payload.description: Downloaded github.com/BLAKE2/BLAKE2's testvectors/blake2-kat.json directly (3072 entries covering blake2b/blake2s/blake2bp/blake2sp/blake2xb/blake2xs, unkeyed and keyed, at every input length 0..255).
payload.result: Verified its unkeyed entries reproduce node:crypto's blake2b512/blake2s256 output exactly, confirming the file's authenticity. Used its keyed entries (which Node cannot verify here) as an independent oracle, including block-boundary lengths 63/64/65 (BLAKE2s) and 127/128/129 (BLAKE2b), both keyed and unkeyed.

payload.description: Downloaded golang.org/x/crypto's blake2s_test.go and blake2b_test.go raw source directly and located the hashes128 table (BLAKE2s New128: keyed, 16-byte/128-bit output).
payload.result: Obtained an independently published known-answer set for a non-default BLAKE2s output length combined with keying, which neither Node nor the default-length KAT file could cover.

payload.description: Used Python 3.14's hashlib.blake2b (an independent CPython C-extension implementation) to generate cross-check values for several non-default BLAKE2b output lengths (1, 16, 20, 48 bytes) and a keyed+short-output combination.
payload.result: All matched my implementation on first try. Noted hashlib.blake2s crashes with an 'Illegal instruction' in this specific environment (reproducible across hashlib.blake2s(), hashlib.new('blake2s'), and the raw _blake2.blake2s C extension) -- an unrelated native-code bug in this Python build, not something to route BLAKE2s output-length verification through; used the Go KAT for that instead.

payload.description: Implemented SHA-512 and SHA-384 from scratch per FIPS 180-4 (sections 4.2.3, 5.3.4, 5.3.5, 6.4, 6.5): 64-bit words as BigInt with a 64-bit mask, DataView for big-endian word I/O and 128-bit length padding. Exports sha512, sha384, sha512Hex, sha384Hex. No cryptographic library imports.
payload.result: File created; later verified against node:crypto and hardcoded FIPS/NIST vectors with 0 failures.

payload.description: Implemented BLAKE2b (64-bit, BigInt) and BLAKE2s (32-bit, Uint32Array) from scratch per RFC 7693: shared SIGMA schedule, per-width G mixing function and F compression function, RFC 3.3 block/padding/counter logic including the keyed and empty-message special cases. Exports blake2b, blake2s, blake2bKeyed, blake2sKeyed. No cryptographic library imports.
payload.result: File created; later verified against node:crypto plus RFC7693/blake2-kat.json/Go/Python-derived KAT with 0 failures.

payload.description: Wrote the test harness: node:crypto cross-check over 11 messages (empty, 'abc', NIST 112-char message, padding-threshold and block-size boundaries at +/-1 byte, million-'a' stress vector) x {sha512,sha384}, plus an 8-entry hardcoded FIPS 180-4/NIST known-answer section. Prints 'N pass, M fail' and exits 1 on failure, matching sha256.test.mjs.

Wrote the test harness: node:crypto cross-check over 12 messages (incl. both algorithms' block boundaries at +/-1 byte and a stress vector) x {blake2b,blake2s}, keyed-vs-unkeyed and outLen-changes-the-whole-digest sanity assertions, plus a 27-entry hardcoded known-answer section spanning RFC 7693 Appendix A/B, the official blake2-kat.json (unkeyed and keyed, several lengths), Go's New128 vectors, and Python-hashlib-derived BLAKE2b vectors at output lengths 1/16/20/32/48 bytes. Prints 'N pass, M fail' and exits 1 on failure.

payload.result: 36 pass, 0 fail. ~10.7s wall time (dominated by the two million-character stress-vector runs under BigInt arithmetic).
